# Avante CN8 side-geometry regression fixture

This regression case captures a poster that broadly reproduced the new front fascia but simplified the side body too much.

## What the failed poster got relatively right

- thin upper front lighting signature
- separated lower lamp / black bumper architecture
- overall new-generation front-end impression

## What must not be accepted

The vehicle should fail validation if the researched real car has pronounced geometric body surfacing but the generated result shows:

- a front fender that flows too smoothly into the front door
- weak or missing front-fender shoulder volume
- a rear quarter panel that narrows like a generic sedan instead of forming a strong outward fender volume
- flattened rear wheel-arch / quarter-panel relationship
- door surfaces simplified into one smooth plane
- missing or weakened geometric character-line intersections
- side sculpting that is cosmetically clean but less three-dimensional than the real vehicle

## Regression rule

A correct-looking front fascia is not sufficient to pass the anchor.

For vehicles such as the new-generation Avante CN8, side/profile and rear-three-quarter evidence must be used to validate the front and rear fenders, wheel arches, door planes and rear-quarter volume.
